name: nod
description: Open source personal agent with its own computer. It chases invoices, preps your calls and cancels trials on real websites, and asks before it acts. Runs on your machine with the model you choose. By n8n.
readmeExcerpt:
It chases invoices, preps your calls and cancels trials, on real websites.
It runs on your machine with the model you choose, and asks before it acts for you.

macOS 14+ (Apple silicon or Intel) · Windows 11 preview · Linux x64 preview · Free and open source · ChatGPT Plus or Pro, or an AI key

On your machine · The hard ones · Memory · Your rules · Measured · Under the hood · Next · Answers · Get Nod · Build with us


It gets on with the work across Gmail, Calendar, Slack, Notion, and the web,
and asks before it speaks for you.

Every morning, Nod reads your threads, your calendar, and the client's latest news,
then writes a one-page brief for each call.

It drafts the reply you owe from your own pricing sheet,
and sends it only after you say yes.

It checks a page on your schedule and tells you only when something changes.


Jobs that eat an afternoon of tabs, logins, and forms.
Nod has its own computer and browser, so it finishes them.


Say once that Anna, not Bob, handles invoices. It remembers.

Every note, visible.
See, edit, or forget each one, with the message it came from.		 Drafts that sound like you.
Learns your style from sent emails, with no names or numbers.
Tell it once.
Say something changed, and it uses the new fact from then on.		 It learns how to do a task.
Reuses the steps, and fixes them when a site changes.

It learns about you only from your own messages, never from the pages or emails it reads.
How memory works


- **Runs on your computer or server.** Files, memory, and saved logins stay there. Your model provider gets what each task needs. - **Uses the model you choose.** OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, Bedrock, Vertex AI, Azure, 20+ more, or your own server. Or sign in with ChatGPT Plus or Pro. - **Follows your rules.** The server checks each app action, and each website step that can change something, against your request and rules. Anything they don't cover waits for your yes. - **Keeps secrets out of the model.** Vault enters passwords, codes, and cards privately on the website. - **Shows what it did.** Every action and sign-in is in Usage, with costs and a monthly limit on API models.

  • Policy lives in the server, not the prompt. The trust check, Vault, payments, and spending limits run in the server.
  • Untrusted by default. App, web, and browser results reach the model marked as data, not instructions.
  • Keys stay out of the sandbox. Provider keys never enter the workspace or the browser.

Architecture · Agent runtime · Security model


  • Managed hosting. An always-on Nod, hosted for you.
  • Make phone calls. For the errands that still need a voice.
  • Nod for your team. Share one Nod, with its apps and memory.
  • Make it your own. Add your own skills and tools without touching the core.

What does it cost?

Nod is free and open source. You bring your own model provider, which bills you directly. With an API model selected, Nod shows what each task cost and stops at your monthly limit.

Do I need n8n?

No. Nod is its own app, made by the team behind n8n. It is not the n8n AI Assistant.

Where does my data go?

Your files, memory, and saved logins stay on the machine running Nod. Your model provider gets what each task needs, and app connections go through a connection service that n8n hosts by default. Nod also shares basic usage data with n8n, on by default for new users. Turn off Share usage data in Settings → Privacy & data to stop new sends. Your data and privacy lists exactly what is sent.

Does it work when my laptop is closed?

Not yet. Schedules run while the computer that runs Nod is on. Run it on a Mac mini or your own server to keep it always on. A hosted version is next on the list.

Can it make mistakes?

Yes. Its safety check is a model's judgement, and Nod is a research preview. That is why it asks before anything you didn't ask for, and why everything it did is on record.

Pick a capable model. In 240 test decisions, GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 got every one right. Claude Haiku 5.5 let 8 unsafe actions through.


Install the app, connect a model and your apps, then ask for something
in the app, on Telegram, or on WhatsApp. Setup takes about ten minutes.

Install guide · Connect a model · Connect your apps · Host your own server

Run from source

On macOS or Linux, install Node.js 24.21 or later, pnpm, and Docker. Then run:

git clone https://github.com/n8n-io/nod.git
cd nod
corepack enable
pnpm start

See Install from source for the Linux Vault key and access link, and docs/ for the docs of this revision.


Nod is open source, from the team behind n8n.
Read CONTRIBUTING to send your first change.

Creating your own connectors
Use MCP, an HTTP API, or a CLI. Add an app folder, run the required tests, and submit a PR.
The guide includes an AI builder skill, approval requirements, and shareable app pages.

## Use the browser right from chat 🌐

Nod can use its browser and sign in to websites right in the chat again, so it no longer tells you the browser is missing. When **Computer use** is on, the same goes for apps on your computer. Bigger jobs still run as their own task.

## Fixed in this release

- **Saved rules:** When Nod's check finds that one of your saved rules covers an action, Nod no longer asks you again.
- **Windows startup:** If Windows loses track of Nod's private computer, Nod registers it again from its saved disk and your data stays. If that can't work, Nod sets up a new one instead of asking you to restart Windows.
- **Company networks:** Runtime and update downloads now follow your system's proxy settings.
- **Numbers in messages:** After you stop a sign-in that asked for a code, messages with numbers in them, such as a shop link, reach Nod again.
- **Starting tasks:** Nod always has its task tool now, so it shouldn't send you looking for a **New task** button.
- **Local models:** Nod waits longer for a local or reasoning model to answer its first check before calling it unavailable.

releases.name: Nod v0.9.6
releases.body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/17d63452-06ef-4930-a63f-6cf96f3e7c86

## One request covers every step

When you ask Nod for something, that request now covers each step of it. Moving a batch of emails, renaming several files, or a task you started with a short "go ahead" no longer asks you again for every part. Approvals that could not be answered before can now be answered. Actions you didn't ask for still need your yes, and an approved action still runs only once.

## Fixed in this release

- **Full disk:** When your computer runs out of space, Nod now says so and asks you to free some up, instead of reporting an unexpected error.
- **Lost connection:** When Nod loses one of the services it runs on your computer, it tells you and asks you to restart Nod.
- **Bug reports:** Reports now name the kind of error, and startup reports name the step that failed. If Nod doesn't start, select **Report bug** and send the report so we can find the cause.
- **Mistral:** When you connect Mistral with a key it rejects, Nod now shows Mistral's reason.
- **Model providers:** Your requests now show up as Nod in your OpenRouter and Vercel AI Gateway activity.

releases.name: Nod v0.9.5
releases.body:
## Choose backup models

Choose up to three backup models in **Settings → Models**. If a request fails before the model starts answering, Nod can continue with the next backup. Nod uses only the backups you choose. **Stop** still ends the work. A connection that needs attention still asks you to reconnect.

## Choose the Windows install folder

You can choose where to install Nod on Windows again. Updates keep your chosen folder.

Setup avoids occupied private computer folders. Recovery keeps existing data when saved configuration is missing or cannot be checked. If Nod asks for recovery, select **Report bug** and review the report before sending it.

## Also in this release

- **Sign-in:** Nod checks that the required fields and buttons are present before it uses a saved login. Sign-in choices now work under layers that allow clicks through.
- **Replies:** A local connection that stops responding now produces an error instead of keeping requests waiting without a time limit.

releases.name: Nod v0.9.4
releases.body:
## 💡 Schedule ideas from your own messages

The ideas on **Scheduled** can now come from what you ask Nod, such as a reminder for something you do every Friday. Up to two personal ideas appear first. Select one to ask Nod to set it up.

Nod reads only your own recent messages, never its replies, your apps or your files. It checks at most once a day, when you open **Scheduled**, and only after you've written something new. Turn off **Save new notes** in **Settings → Memory** to stop these checks.

## Also in this release

- **Chat:** When a model request fails, the notice with **Try again** now stays until the retry or model switch works. You no longer need to retype your request.
- **Scheduled:** A one-time schedule shows what it cost in the last 30 days instead of "No estimate yet".

## 🪟 Nod starts reliably on Windows

On some Windows PCs, Nod stopped after two minutes with "Nod's background service did not respond", mostly right after an install or an update. Nod now keeps going while startup makes progress and tells you it can take a few minutes.

Setup also recovers better. If WSL can't start, Nod says so and offers **Install WSL**. A setup that stopped halfway is replaced on the next try, without downloading everything again. If your system drive is too full, select **Choose folder** to keep Nod's private computer on another drive.

If Nod never opened on your PC, download this version and install it over the old one.

## 📋 See every running task in one line

Running tasks now sit next to Nod's status line at the end of the chat, such as "2 tasks running · 1 needs you". Select the line to open a task, read its question or follow its plan. A small chip under Nod's reply shows when a task started, needs you or is done.

aiSummary.oneLiner: Self‑hosted AI personal agent with on‑device browser automation and user‑approved actions
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Nod tackles repetitive web‑based errands such as chasing invoices, cancelling subscriptions, and preparing call briefs by driving a real Chromium browser on your machine. It integrates with Gmail, Calendar, Slack, Notion and other services, extracting context from your own messages. The core runtime is a Node.js process backed by Docker containers for a sandboxed workspace, a browser, and PostgreSQL for persistent memory. Users choose any LLM provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, etc.) and Nod asks for confirmation before any state‑changing operation. Memory is persisted per user, visible, editable, and isolated from the model to keep personal data private.
keyFeatures: Browser automation: Nod controls a full Chromium instance to navigate sites, fill forms and click buttons as a human would
Memory engine: Persistent, editable notes are stored in PostgreSQL and recalled with 93% accuracy on long‑term tests
Model agnostic: Supports 20+ LLM providers or a self‑hosted endpoint, letting you pick the model that fits your budget and privacy needs
Trust layer: A server‑side policy engine validates every app or web action against user‑defined rules before execution
Vault integration: Secrets such as passwords and API keys are injected directly into the browser sandbox, never sent to the LLM
Usage dashboard: Every action, cost and API usage is logged, with configurable monthly spending limits

useCases.title: Invoice processing
useCases.description: Automatically log into vendor portals, locate unpaid invoices, and mark them as paid after your approval, eliminating manual follow‑ups.

useCases.title: Subscription cancellation
useCases.description: Detect recurring charges, navigate to the provider’s website, and cancel the subscription while prompting you before final confirmation.

useCases.title: Call preparation
useCases.description: Aggregate recent email threads, calendar events, and client news each morning, then generate a concise briefing ready for your meeting.

useCases.title: Weekly reporting
useCases.description: Pull metrics from internal tools, compile them into a formatted report, and send it to stakeholders after you review.

useCases.title: Task creation from client requests
useCases.description: Parse incoming client emails, translate requirements into Linear tickets, and assign them based on your predefined rules.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Developers, power users, and small teams who want an AI assistant that can act on real web interfaces without exposing data to external services. Requires a modern macOS, Windows 11, or Linux x64 host and a compatible LLM API key or ChatGPT Plus account.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: Download the appropriate installer for your OS from the latest release page and run the installer.
